packages/Common.reason: node-forge has no fixed release: <= 1.4.0 is affected and 1.4.0 is the latest (the advisory was widened to it on 2026-10-01; checked again on 2026-10-25, when the advisory still listed no patched version). It comes in only through acme-client 5.4.0, the latest acme-client (still depending on node-forge ^1.3.1 on 2026-10-25), which loads it for its legacy forge API. OneUptime calls acme.crypto (createCsr, readCertificateInfo in Common/Server/Utils/Greenlock/Greenlock.ts), which is built on Node's crypto and @peculiar/x509, and acme-client's forge module only generates keys and signs CSRs: nothing here verifies an RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature with node-forge, which is where the advisory's forged signatures are accepted.

packages/MobileApp.reason: node-forge has no fixed release: <= 1.4.0 is affected and 1.4.0 is the latest (checked again on 2026-10-25). It comes in only through Expo's developer tooling, @expo/cli and @expo/code-signing-certificates (0.0.7, the latest, still depends on node-forge ^1.4.0 on 2026-10-25), which run in Node on the developer's machine and are not bundled into the app. Their node-forge verify calls check a signature they have just made, or the developer's own certificate or CSR, never one an attacker supplies, so the forged signatures the advisory is about never reach them.

zod has no fixed 3.x release: every version below 4.6.6 is affected and 3.25.76 is the latest 3.x. It comes in only through Expo's developer tooling, @expo/cli 57.0.32: every @expo/cli still requires zod ^3.25.76, the newest (58.1.15) included (checked on 2026-10-25). @expo/cli runs in Node on the developer's machine and is not bundled into the app; it validates the developer's own project configuration and dev tools plugins, never input from an attacker. packages/Common moved to zod 4 on 2026-10-25 and has no zod 3 left.
